Aggregate Hospital-Profile Counts Under Discrete Missing-Data Allocation

Source: R/profile_aggregate_counts_allocation.R
profile_aggregate_counts_with_allocation.Rd

A complete event's compatible-state set is always a single state (see profile_estimate's "missing_allocation" doc), so it deterministically allocates to its own true state on every draw – there is no need to separately add an "n_observed" term. Passing complete AND partial events together (the same convention profile_aggregate_for_daly already uses) reproduces the observed count automatically, with the partial events' allocation uncertainty layered on top.

Usage

profile_aggregate_counts_with_allocation(
  est,
  ids,
  pathogen,
  cohort_definition,
  sampler_check = NULL,
  ci_level = 0.95,
  min_n_events = 10L,
  min_n_draws = 100L
)

Arguments

est

List from profile_estimate with estimand = "missing_allocation" (reads $allocated_state, $state_labels).

ids

Data frame with a group column, same row order/length as the Y passed to profile_estimate (one row per event).

pathogen, cohort_definition

Character, echoed into the output for provenance (same convention as profile_aggregate_for_daly).

sampler_check

List or NULL. Same convention as profile_aggregate_for_daly: reads $status; "pass" is the only acceptable value, anything else (including NULL) makes every row ineligible with a named reason.

ci_level

Numeric in (0, 1). Quantile interval level for the realised-count distribution. Default 0.95.

min_n_events, min_n_draws

Integer floors below which a group x profile row is marked ineligible (same meaning as profile_aggregate_for_daly). Defaults 10L, 100L.

Value

Data frame, one row per group x profile: N_mean, N_lower, N_upper (the realised completed-count distribution's mean and ci_level quantile interval – integer-valued draws summarised, not a continuous proportion), n_events, n_draws, n_profile_classes, sampler_status, computational_checks_passed_YLL/ computational_checks_passed_YLD and their exclusion_reason_* (same computational-check logic and column names as profile_aggregate_for_daly, for a consistent downstream filter regardless of which aggregator produced a row – and see that function's doc for what these flags do NOT establish: PPC adequacy, held-out validation, missingness sensitivity, death/ episode attribution, double counting, or RR/duration/disability input availability. This is a computational pre-check, not a burden-use release decision.), and estimator = "joint_bernoulli_discrete_allocation" so the two aggregators' outputs are never silently confused if concatenated.

Details

For hospital/group \(h\) and profile \(s\), at each posterior draw \(m\): $$N_{hs}^{(m)} = \sum_{e \in h} I(\mathrm{allocated\_state}[m, e] = s)$$ Collecting \(N_{hs}^{(1)}, \ldots, N_{hs}^{(M)}\) gives the realised completed-count distribution for that hospital/profile; this function reports its mean and ci_level quantile interval. This single procedure automatically mixes parameter uncertainty (the draw-to-draw allocation weights shift because \(\theta^{(m)}\) shifts) and allocation uncertainty (even at fixed weights, which specific state gets drawn is itself random) – the two-term variance decomposition discussed alongside this function's design, obtained here by direct simulation rather than a closed-form formula.
